messages:
maya: hey team — putting up a small quickstart: next-edge agent starter that wires Redwood SDK + LangChain agents. Ran into weird auth parity: node SDK refresh flow works but the browser/edge runtime fails to retry on 401s.
jordan: can you paste the error?
maya: sure:
```
Error: Request failed with status 401
  at retry (/workspace/node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/index.js:120:15)
  at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:95:5)
```
sam: which SDK version and bundle target?
maya: @sam using redwood-sdk 0.14.2-edge. The same code in node reattaches Authorization after refresh, but the browser bundle's fetch wrapper drops the header on redirect so retry loop never refreshes.
chloe: hm, we have middleware that strips auth on cross-origin redirects. Is this the quickstart repo or the new agent starter? share link pls.
maya: repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-agent-quickstart (internal). Starter README currently tells users to set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env.local, but our devex eval-harness docs use ephemeral user tokens + refresh server. Docs drift is causing onboarding confusion.
jordan: OK can you repro with minimal steps? e.g., start `pnpm dev`, visit /agent, then trigger a model call while rotating the key to force 401.
maya: repro gist pasted in thread — includes a small script that forces token expiry. Steps are short.
devex-bot: CI: failed job — e2e/netlify for PR #224 — snapshot mismatch on /agent (build 6421).
sam: digging in — core issue looks like the browser fetch retry logic reuses the original Request object, which in some runtimes loses manual headers on redirect. Quickfix: when retrying, reconstruct the request and reattach the current token from the token store instead of copying headers from the failed request.
chloe: sounds right. Also we should update starter README to surface "ephemeral token" vs "static key" modes and link to eval-harness runbook. New users hit this fast and give up.
jordan: can we add an integration test that simulates token expiry and asserts the retry path refreshes and re-sends the request? maybe use msw + fake timers so it's deterministic.
maya: i'll add a minimal test in the starter that simulates expiry and verifies model call eventually returns 200. pairing with @sam tomorrow.
sam: opened PR #229: reattach-token-on-retry + e2e test + README tweaks. initial CI failing due to a flaky setTimeout in the test.
jordan: nit: prefer using jest.useFakeTimers()/advanceTimersByTime to avoid flakes. also add a telemetry counter (auth_retries_failed) so we can alert on rollout regressions.
maya: agreed — updating tests to use fake timers and adding the telemetry metric.
chloe: thanks, this will reduce onboarding friction for the Next starter and the LangChain agent example. after green, let's backport the fix to the other samplekits (vite/react, edge-sample).
sam: will merge after test fix and one more review.
maya: thanks everyone :thumbsup: — also adding a short PR note in the starter README about recommended local dev patterns (use static key for quick local iteration, ephemeral tokens for eval/CI).
jordan: one follow-up: can we add a tiny troubleshooting section in the eval-harness that explains how to reproduce token rotation and what telemetry/trace to look for? new hires keep hitting this.
chloe: good call. i'll add a short subsection under "Auth & Tokens".
sam: PR updated. running CI.
devex-bot: CI: PR #229 passed all checks (build 6480) :white_check_mark:
maya: awesome — merging and prepping a small announcement in devex docs channel with a link to the quickstart patch and the test case so other starters can copy it.
jordan: perfect. thanks for moving fast on this.
maya: np — will follow up with a tiny workshop doc for new hires to exercise the agent starter and the eval harness.
